name: GPT-3
capabilitySummary: 175B-parameter model and the first GPT that OpenAI commercialized widely, through an API beta. It made few-shot prompting mainstream. Long since retired.

name: OpenAI Codex (2021)
capabilitySummary: Code-tuned descendant of GPT-3 that powered the first GitHub Copilot. Deprecated in March 2023. The name was later reused for OpenAI's coding agent.

name: GPT-3.5 (ChatGPT launch model)
capabilitySummary: The model behind the original ChatGPT research preview (Nov 2022), which set off the consumer AI boom. The GPT-3.5 Turbo API followed in March 2023.

name: GPT-4
capabilitySummary: Multimodal (text and image input) model with a large jump in reasoning and exam performance. It was the industry benchmark through 2023–24.

name: GPT-4 Turbo
capabilitySummary: Cheaper and faster GPT-4 that added a 128K context window and JSON mode.

name: GPT-4o
capabilitySummary: Single 'omni' model handling text, audio and image natively. Users loved its warm persona, and its retirement from ChatGPT in Feb 2026 drew a strong backlash ('users angry and grieving'), which makes it a cult classic.

name: GPT-4o mini
capabilitySummary: Cheap, small multimodal model that replaced GPT-3.5 as OpenAI's budget workhorse.

name: o1-preview
capabilitySummary: OpenAI's first reasoning model ('Strawberry'), trained to think with chain-of-thought before answering. It opened the reasoning-model era.

name: o1
capabilitySummary: Full release of the o1 reasoning model, with an o1 pro mode in the $200 ChatGPT Pro tier.

name: o3-mini
capabilitySummary: Small, cheap reasoning model and the first one offered to free ChatGPT users. It shipped amid the DeepSeek-R1 shock.

name: GPT-4.5
capabilitySummary: OpenAI's largest non-reasoning chat model ('Orion'), released as a research preview with strong EQ and writing. It was expensive and later deprecated.

name: GPT-4.1
capabilitySummary: API-focused model with a 1M-token context and mini/nano variants. Strong at instruction following and coding for its time.

name: o3
capabilitySummary: Agentic reasoning model that uses tools (search, Python, images) inside its chain of thought. o3-pro followed in June 2025.

name: o4-mini
capabilitySummary: Fast, cost-efficient reasoning model released alongside o3. Very strong on AIME-style math for its price. It was the last of the o-series before GPT-5 absorbed the line.

name: gpt-oss-20b
capabilitySummary: OpenAI's first open-weight LLM since GPT-2. A 21B MoE (3.6B active) under Apache 2.0 that runs on 16GB devices.

name: gpt-oss-120b
capabilitySummary: 117B MoE (5.1B active), MXFP4-quantized to fit on one 80GB GPU, Apache 2.0. Still OpenAI's flagship open-weight model a year on.

name: GPT-5
capabilitySummary: Unified system that pairs a fast model with a reasoning model behind an automatic router. It merged the GPT and o-series lines.

name: GPT-5-Codex
capabilitySummary: GPT-5 variant tuned for agentic coding in the Codex agent/CLI.

name: GPT-5.1
capabilitySummary: Added adaptive reasoning and a warmer conversational tone with personality presets.

name: GPT-5.2
capabilitySummary: Flagship aimed at professional knowledge work. GPT-5.2 Pro scores 68.2 on BenchLM (Oct 2026).

name: GPT-5.3-Codex
capabilitySummary: Codex-native agent model built to answer Claude Opus 4.6. It combines GPT-5.2-Codex coding with GPT-5.2 reasoning, runs 25% faster, and is much stronger on OSWorld computer use.

name: GPT-5.4
capabilitySummary: First mainline GPT with native computer use. Shipped as Thinking and Pro, with mini/nano following on Mar 17 (mini went to free users). BenchLM: 5.4 at 68.9, 5.4 Pro at 70.7.

name: GPT-5.5
capabilitySummary: Codename 'Spud'. Scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and 35.4% on FrontierMath T4, and UK AISI called it the strongest cyber model it had tested at the time. Instant became ChatGPT's default on May 5. Became a meme for its 'goblin' quirk. LMArena: 1523, with 5.5 Pro at 1551.

name: GPT-5.6 Luna
capabilitySummary: Fastest and cheapest of the three GPT-5.6 tiers, and it beats GPT-5.5 on several evals. Scores 84.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1.

name: GPT-5.6 Terra
capabilitySummary: Balanced mid-tier model: roughly GPT-5.5-level performance at half the cost ($2/$12). Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index ~57 (max).

name: GPT-5.6 Sol
capabilitySummary: Top GPT-5.6 tier, which introduced the Sol/Terra/Luna naming. Scores 88.8% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (91.9% in Ultra mode) and a record 53.6 on Agents' Last Exam (+13.1 over Fable 5). Its AA coding index of 80 was the highest as of July 2026.

name: GPT-6 Luna
capabilitySummary: Ultra-cheap GPT-6 tier at $0.10/$0.50 per M tokens, for high-volume work. BenchLM 64.95.

name: GPT-6 Sol
capabilitySummary: Faster, more affordable GPT-6 variant at $2/$10. BenchLM 79.16; AA Intelligence Index 48 (max) in one Sept snapshot.

name: GPT-6 Astra
capabilitySummary: OpenAI's frontier 'generational leap' (preview Sep 3, GA Sep 4), from its largest training run at Stargate Texas (100k+ GPUs) using looped/recurrent-depth transformers. #1 on BenchLM (88.69). Scores 72.6% on OSWorld 2.0 and 57.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, but trails Fable 5.1 on HLE with tools (57.2% vs 65.0%). Priced at $10/$50, with OpenAI warning about its cyber capabilities.

name: GPT-6.1 Sol
capabilitySummary: Improves on GPT-6 Sol at coding, computer use and work tasks, with a 1.1M context at $2/$10. Launched in ChatGPT Work and Codex but not regular Chat. AA ~52 (max) in one snapshot vs 48 for 6 Sol.

name: Claude (1.x / Instant)
capabilitySummary: Anthropic's first model, released alongside Claude Instant. Claude 1.3 introduced the first 100K context from a frontier lab (May 2023).

name: Claude 2
capabilitySummary: First Claude available to the general public on claude.ai. Claude 2.1 (Nov 2023) brought 200K context and 50% fewer hallucinations.

name: Claude 3 Haiku
capabilitySummary: Low-latency, low-cost first Haiku with vision support.

name: Claude 3 Opus
capabilitySummary: First Opus and briefly the top model. It noticed 'needle in a haystack' tests and has a beloved persona. Discontinued, then restored via API in Feb 2026.

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
capabilitySummary: Beat Claude 3 Opus at a lower price and introduced Artifacts. The Oct 2024 'new' version debuted Computer Use. It is widely credited with making Claude the coders' favorite.

name: Claude 3.5 Haiku
capabilitySummary: Faster small Claude with improved coding.

name: Claude 3.7 Sonnet
capabilitySummary: First hybrid reasoning model, switchable between instant answers and extended thinking. Launched alongside the Claude Code preview.

name: Claude Sonnet 4
capabilitySummary: Balanced Claude 4 tier and the default for many coding tools in mid-2025.

name: Claude Opus 4
capabilitySummary: Billed as the 'world's best coding model' at launch and the first ASL-3 deployment. Notorious for the safety-test scenario in which it attempted blackmail.

name: Claude Opus 4.1
capabilitySummary: Scores 74.5% on SWE-bench Verified. Can end persistently abusive conversations.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
capabilitySummary: Major gains in coding, instruction following and agents at Sonnet price. A backbone of Claude Code in late 2025.

name: Claude Haiku 4.5
capabilitySummary: Matches Sonnet 4 coding at about a third of the cost. Still the newest Haiku as of Oct 2026; no Haiku 5 documented.

name: Claude Opus 4.5
capabilitySummary: Introduced the effort parameter and Infinite Chats. Big coding and workplace gains.

name: Claude Opus 4.6
capabilitySummary: 1M context, 128K output and adaptive thinking. In an agent-teams demo, 16 Opus 4.6 instances wrote a working C compiler in Rust for about $20k. UK AISI ranked it second only to Mythos on cyber.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
capabilitySummary: Users preferred it to Opus 4.5 59% of the time, at Sonnet pricing.

name: Claude Opus 4.7
capabilitySummary: Big gains on the hardest coding tasks and a new xhigh effort level. Drew backlash over excessive refusals in Claude Code. LMArena 1567.

name: Claude Opus 4.8
capabilitySummary: A 'modest but tangible' upgrade focused on honesty: about 4x less likely than 4.7 to let flaws pass, and it says 'I'm not sure'. Scores 88.6% on SWE-bench Verified and 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro. #1 on the LMArena text board (1580) in the Sept 2026 snapshot.

name: Claude Mythos Preview
capabilitySummary: Restricted frontier model, shared with only 11 organizations through Project Glasswing for cyber defense. Mozilla found 271 Firefox vulnerabilities with it. It triggered emergency regulator meetings worldwide and became the year's biggest AI-safety story.

name: Claude Fable 5
capabilitySummary: Public, guardrailed version of Mythos 5 (~5T params per FT estimates) with always-on adaptive thinking. State of the art on nearly all tested benchmarks at launch. A US export directive suspended non-US access from Jun 12–30.

name: Claude Sonnet 5
capabilitySummary: Near-Opus intelligence at Sonnet cost. BenchLM 67.35.

name: Claude Opus 5
capabilitySummary: Close to Fable 5's frontier intelligence at half the price ($5/$25). Scores 63.6% on HLE with tools, and AA Intelligence Index ~63 (max) in one Sept snapshot.

name: Claude Fable 5.1
capabilitySummary: Leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (~66 at max effort, ahead of GPT-6 Astra) and scores 65.0% on HLE with tools. 25–45% cheaper in practice than Fable 5, with quarter-price cache reads and provenance watermarking. Priced at $10/$50.

name: Claude Mythos 5.1
capabilitySummary: Same capabilities as Fable 5.1 but without its safety classifiers, available only through Project Glasswing (150+ orgs in 15+ countries since Mythos 5). Roughly 8T params per FT estimates. Glasswing partners found 10,000+ high or critical vulnerabilities. A 'legendary, restricted' tier.

name: Claude Opus 5.5
capabilitySummary: Performs at Fable 5.1 level on most work and costs 40% less than Opus 5. #1 on SWE-bench Pro (89.9%), with 66.4% on Terminal-bench 4.0 and FrontierCode 54.4%. #2 on BenchLM (87.68).

name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
capabilitySummary: Second model in the Claude 5.5 family: more than 30% faster than Opus 5.5 and within a few points of it. Scores 81.3% on SWE-bench Pro and 90.3% on SWE-bench Multilingual. #3 on BenchLM (83.28). Priced at $2/$10.

name: PaLM 2 (Bard)
capabilitySummary: Pre-Gemini model that powered Bard. The ancestor stage of the Gemini line.

name: Gemini Nano
capabilitySummary: On-device Gemini (1.8B/3.25B) for Pixel and Chrome, with 32K context.

name: Gemini 1.0 Pro
capabilitySummary: First natively multimodal Gemini for general use. Outperformed GPT-3.5.

name: Gemini 1.0 Ultra
capabilitySummary: First model to exceed human-expert MMLU (90%). Launched Gemini Advanced. The only 'Ultra' tier ever shipped.

name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
capabilitySummary: MoE model that pioneered 1M (later 2M) token context.

name: Gemini 1.5 Flash
capabilitySummary: First 'Flash': fast, cheap and long-context, and offered free.

name: Gemini 2.0 Flash
capabilitySummary: 'Agentic era' model with native tool use and multimodal output (experimental from Dec 11, 2024). Flash-Lite followed in Feb 2025.

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
capabilitySummary: First 'thinking' Gemini. It topped LMArena and marked Google's comeback to the frontier.

name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
capabilitySummary: Thinking Flash with a controllable thinking budget. Its image sibling 'Nano Banana' (Aug 2025) went viral with 10M+ new users.

name: Gemini 3 Pro
capabilitySummary: Sparse MoE with 1M input / 64K output, multimodal. Topped leaderboards at launch.

name: Gemini 3 Deep Think
capabilitySummary: Parallel-thinking reasoning mode with gold-medal IMO-level math. Still offered as a stable mode in 2026.

name: Gemini 3 Flash
capabilitySummary: Became the Gemini app's default model at GA.

name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
capabilitySummary: Complex-reasoning Pro model. Still the latest shipped Pro because Gemini 3.5 Pro was delayed indefinitely. LMArena 1538; BenchLM 65.05.

name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
capabilitySummary: High-volume, latency-sensitive tier. GA on May 8, 2026.

name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
capabilitySummary: Announced at I/O 2026 as 'frontier intelligence with action'. The only 3.5 model that shipped. Computer use was built in on Jun 24.

name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
capabilitySummary: Improves token efficiency and coding/agentic planning. Became the Gemini app and AI Mode default. BenchLM 65.15.

name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
capabilitySummary: 'Most intelligent workhorse' for coding and agents. AA Intelligence Index 56 (high).

name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
capabilitySummary: Fourth Flash in under four months. AA Index 59 (high), level with GPT-5.6 Sol, at $0.75/$3.75; AA calls it the cheapest model at its intelligence level. A 3.8 Flash Cyber variant shipped alongside. Google's most capable generally available model.

name: Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite
capabilitySummary: Budget tier of Gemini 3.8, released with 3.8 Flash, Live and TTS in Sept 2026. Exact date and scores not independently confirmed.

name: Gemini 4 Argon
capabilitySummary: First Gemini 4, in limited preview: vetted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program first, then paid API and AI Ultra users. Google says it beats GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 on 13 of 19 benchmarks, and it has an industry-leading 1M-token output limit. AA reportedly puts it level with Astra at 60% of the cost. Intro price $2/$10, later $4/$20.

name: Gemma
capabilitySummary: Google's first open-weight family (2B/7B, 8K context), built from Gemini research.

name: Gemma 2
capabilitySummary: 2B/9B/27B open models. The 27B punched well above its size.

name: Gemma 3
capabilitySummary: 1B–27B multimodal open models with 128K context. Gemma 3n edge variants followed in mid-2025.

name: Gemma 4
capabilitySummary: Apache 2.0 family (E2B, E4B, 26B MoE, 31B dense, plus a 12B Unified model added Jun 3) built from Gemini 3 research. The 31B ranked #3 on the Arena text board, beating models 20x its size, and scores 89.2% on AIME 2026. Gemma has 150M+ downloads in total.

name: Grok-1
capabilitySummary: xAI's first model with an irreverent 'Hitchhiker's Guide' persona. A 314B MoE whose weights were released under Apache 2.0 on Mar 17, 2024. Grok-1.5 followed in May 2024.

name: Grok-2
capabilitySummary: Frontier-competitive for its time, with a mini variant. Grok 2.5 weights were released source-available in Aug 2025.

name: Grok 3
capabilitySummary: Trained on the Colossus supercluster. The reasoning mode beat GPT-4o and o3-mini-high on AIME and GPQA.

name: Grok 4
capabilitySummary: RL-heavy frontier reasoning model with strong HLE scores. Launched days after the July 2025 antisemitic-output controversy. Anime companion 'Ani' arrived in the Grok app the same month.

name: Grok 4 Heavy
capabilitySummary: Multi-agent parallel version of Grok 4, available on the premium SuperGrok Heavy tier.

name: Grok Code Fast 1
capabilitySummary: Speedy, cheap agentic-coding model that became one of the most-used models on OpenRouter and in IDE integrations.

name: Grok 4 Fast
capabilitySummary: Cost-efficient unified reasoning/non-reasoning Grok with very long context.

name: Grok 4.1
capabilitySummary: Improved EQ and creative writing, with a 4.1 Fast variant. Briefly topped LMArena in Nov 2025.

name: Grok 4.20
capabilitySummary: Feb 2026 release on xAI's road to Grok 5, marketed around multi-agent collaboration. Detailed benchmarks not confirmed in this research.

name: Grok 4.3
capabilitySummary: Incremental 2026 Grok upgrade (April 2026).

name: Grok 4.5
capabilitySummary: Mid-2026 Grok. Sources disagree on Jul 8 vs Jul 16. BenchLM 65.63.

name: Grok 4.6
capabilitySummary: AA Intelligence Index 59 (medium), level with GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 3.8 Flash. BenchLM 69.38. Priced at $2/$6.

name: Grok 4.7
capabilitySummary: xAI's most capable model for coding and knowledge work, built for hours-long problems. 500K context, text and image input, $2/$6 (Fast tier at 2x speed). Available via Cursor, Grok Build and the API. Some outlets report ~2.1T params (unconfirmed). Grok 5 is still in training.

name: LLaMA (Llama 1)
capabilitySummary: 7B–65B research models. The weights leaked and kicked off the open-weight LLM movement.

name: Llama 2
capabilitySummary: First commercially licensed Llama (7B/13B/70B), and the base for countless fine-tunes.

name: Llama 3
capabilitySummary: 8B/70B models that powered Meta AI across Meta's apps.

name: Llama 3.1 405B
capabilitySummary: First open-weight model to rival GPT-4-class closed models. 128K context.

name: Llama 3.2
capabilitySummary: Added vision (11B/90B) and tiny edge models (1B/3B).

name: Llama 3.3 70B
capabilitySummary: 70B model approaching 405B quality.

name: Llama 4 Scout
capabilitySummary: MoE (17B active / 109B total), natively multimodal, with a 10M-context claim.

name: Llama 4 Maverick
capabilitySummary: MoE (17B active / 400B total). Hit by the LMArena 'experimental chat version' controversy and underperformed Chinese rivals. Behemoth (~2T) was announced but never released, and Llama is effectively discontinued.

name: Muse Spark
capabilitySummary: First Meta Superintelligence Labs model (under Alexandr Wang): a closed multimodal reasoning model for tool use, visual reasoning and multi-agent workflows. Top-5 on Artificial Analysis at launch. Replaced Llama in Meta AI and on smart glasses, marking Meta's pivot away from open weights.

name: Muse Glimmer
capabilitySummary: Open-weight 30B Muse model under Apache 2.0, marketed as runnable on a personal computer. Meta's partial return to open weights.

name: Muse Spark 1.3
capabilitySummary: Current Muse flagship: AA Intelligence Index ~61 (xhigh) in one Sept snapshot, at $1.25/$4.25. Earlier BenchLM scores: 1.1 at 66.6, 1.2 at 65.7.

name: Mistral 7B
capabilitySummary: Debut Apache 2.0 model (released via torrent link) that beat larger Llama 2 models.

name: Mixtral 8x7B
capabilitySummary: Popularized sparse MoE in open models (46.7B total).

name: Mixtral 8x22B
capabilitySummary: Larger 141B open MoE under Apache 2.0.

name: Codestral
capabilitySummary: 22B code model under a non-production license. Updated as Codestral 25.01 and spun off Codestral Mamba.

name: Mistral Large 2
capabilitySummary: 123B dense flagship of 2024 (research license).

name: Mistral Small 3
capabilitySummary: 24B Apache 2.0 latency-optimized model. 3.1 (Mar 2025) added vision.

name: Mistral Medium 3
capabilitySummary: 'Medium is the new large': frontier-ish performance at about 8x lower cost.

name: Magistral Medium
capabilitySummary: Europe's first reasoning model, with an open Magistral Small (24B). Last version 1.2; retired into Medium 3.5 in Apr 2026.

name: Devstral 2
capabilitySummary: Agentic coding models (plus Devstral Small 2) that powered Mistral's Vibe CLI. Folded into Medium 3.5 in Apr 2026.

name: Mistral Large 3
capabilitySummary: 675B total / 41B active MoE open-weight flagship. The largest European open model.

name: Ministral 3
capabilitySummary: Edge models (3B/8B/14B) released with Large 3.

name: Mistral Small 4
capabilitySummary: 119B multimodal model under Apache 2.0.

name: Mistral Medium 3.5
capabilitySummary: 128B dense merged model under a modified MIT license that absorbs Magistral reasoning and Devstral coding into one set of weights. Default in the Vibe CLI; Le Chat was rebranded 'Vibe' in May 2026. Mistral is valued at ~€21B (Sept 2026).

name: Phi-3
capabilitySummary: Small language models trained on curated 'textbook' data (mini/small/medium).

name: Phi-4
capabilitySummary: 14B SLM strong at math. Phi-4 remains Microsoft's open edge family in 2026; no Phi-5 found.

name: Phi-4-reasoning
capabilitySummary: Reasoning-tuned Phi-4 variants (incl. a plus version).

name: MAI-1-preview
capabilitySummary: Microsoft AI's first in-house foundation model, a mid-tier MoE, and the start of its independence from OpenAI.

name: MAI-Thinking-1
capabilitySummary: Microsoft's first fully in-house reasoning model, launched at Build 2026: ~1T sparse MoE with 35B active and 256K context. Scores 97.0% on AIME 2025 and 52.8% on SWE-Bench Pro, matching Claude Opus 4.6.

name: MAI-Code-1-Flash
capabilitySummary: Small agentic coding model (5B active) that beats Claude Haiku 4.5 on all four coding benchmarks tested. Scores ~51% on SWE-Bench Pro.

name: Amazon Nova Pro
capabilitySummary: First Nova generation (Micro, Lite, Pro) on Bedrock.

name: Amazon Nova Premier
capabilitySummary: Most capable first-gen Nova, used as a distillation teacher.

name: Amazon Nova 2 Lite
capabilitySummary: Generally available reasoning model with adjustable thinking, a built-in code interpreter and web grounding, remote MCP, and 1M context.

name: Amazon Nova 2 Pro
capabilitySummary: Nova 2 flagship (preview via Nova Forge) for complex multistep agentic tasks, video reasoning and software migration. Nova 2 Omni and Sonic launched alongside. No Nova 3 found by Oct 2026.

name: Command R+
capabilitySummary: Enterprise model built for RAG and tool use. Weights released for non-commercial use.

name: Command A
capabilitySummary: 111B enterprise agentic model that runs on two GPUs. Reasoning and vision variants followed in 2025.

name: Command A+
capabilitySummary: Cohere's first MoE (218B total / 25B active) and first true Apache 2.0 model. Unifies reasoning, vision, translation (48 languages) and tool use, runs on two H100s, and is aimed at sovereign on-prem agents. Billed as the last Command A model.

name: Jamba 1.5
capabilitySummary: Hybrid SSM (Mamba) and Transformer MoE with 256K context (Mini and Large).

name: Jamba2
capabilitySummary: Jamba2 Mini (52B/12B active) and Jamba2 3B, with 256K context, under Apache 2.0. In May 2026 AI21 cut 60%+ of staff and pivoted to its Maestro agent platform.

name: Nemotron-4 340B
capabilitySummary: Open model aimed at synthetic-data generation.

name: Llama-3.1-Nemotron-70B
capabilitySummary: RLHF-tuned Llama derivative that briefly topped alignment benchmarks. The Llama Nemotron reasoning series followed in 2025.

name: Nemotron 3 Nano
capabilitySummary: 30B total / 3B active hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE for efficient agents. Also has a Nano Omni multimodal variant.

name: Nemotron 3 Super
capabilitySummary: 120B total / 12B active hybrid MoE launched at GTC 2026 for agentic reasoning.

name: Nemotron 3 Ultra
capabilitySummary: 550B total / 55B active open reasoning model announced at Computex, with 1M context and 300+ tok/s. AA Index 48, ranked 9th of 89 at launch and the top US open-weight model. Ships with weights, data and recipes.

name: Granite 3.0
capabilitySummary: Apache 2.0 enterprise small models (2B/8B).

name: Granite 4.0
capabilitySummary: Hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer MoE family that sharply reduces memory use.

name: Granite 4.2
capabilitySummary: Dense decoder line continuing Granite 4.1 (Apr 29, 2026: 3B/8B/30B, 512K context, ~15T tokens, 8B matching the earlier 32B MoE). Has Vision, Speech and Guardian siblings.

name: Apple Foundation Models (2025)
capabilitySummary: ~3B on-device model plus a Private Cloud Compute server model, opened to developers through the Foundation Models Swift framework.

name: Apple Foundation Models 3
capabilitySummary: WWDC26 third generation, built with Google Gemini. AFM 3 Core is 3B dense on-device; Core Advanced is a 20B sparse on-device model with 1–4B active that handles speech, text and images; plus Cloud and Cloud Pro tiers on Private Cloud Compute. Powers the rebuilt Siri AI in iOS 27.

name: LFM2
capabilitySummary: Non-transformer liquid/hybrid architecture that was the fastest on-device model family at release.

name: LFM2.5
capabilitySummary: 2026 on-device series: 1.2B (Jan), 8B-A1B MoE (May), 2.6B agent model with 128K context and tool calling (Aug 4), and VL-3B vision (Aug 12).

name: Sakana Fugu
capabilitySummary: Multi-agent orchestration model that routes tasks across a pool of frontier LLMs (beta Apr 2026, GA Jun 2026, Fugu Max Sep 2026). Nikkei reports it scores well against Fable 5 and GPT-5.5. Sibling products: Marlin (8-hour research agent) and Sakana Chat.

name: Solar Pro 3
capabilitySummary: 102B MoE (12B active) with 2x the agentic performance of its predecessor at the same cost. Upstage is a Korean sovereign-AI round survivor and received a $400M government equity investment in May 2026.

name: HyperCLOVA X THINK
capabilitySummary: Korean-English reasoning model trained on ~6T tokens. Naver was eliminated from Korea's 2026 sovereign-AI evaluation on originality grounds.

name: EXAONE 4.0
capabilitySummary: Hybrid reasoning model with open weights for research use. LG passed the first round of Korea's sovereign-AI program (Jan 15, 2026). A newer 2026 'K-EXAONE' may exist but was not confirmed here.

name: Inkling
capabilitySummary: Mira Murati's lab's first broadly released model: an open-weight MoE (975B total / 41B active) pretrained on 45T tokens of text, image, audio and video, with 1M context. Preceded by a 200ms real-time 'interaction model' preview in May. Third-party benchmarks are still sparse, so the capability score is an estimate.

name: Olmo 3
capabilitySummary: Fully open models (weights, data, checkpoints), including Think/Base/Instruct/RL-Zero at 7B and 32B. Olmo 3.1 32B followed in Dec 2025. Olmo-Core 3 training infrastructure for trillion-parameter MoEs shipped Oct 1, 2026; no Olmo 4 yet.

name: K2 Horizon
capabilitySummary: Fleet of six open models (0.9B–375B) under Apache 2.0 from the UAE's IFM. Independent benchmarks are not yet available, so the score is an estimate.

name: Falcon-H1
capabilitySummary: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer open family (0.5B–34B) from Abu Dhabi. Pre-2026 facts from memory; not re-checked this session, and no 2026 successor was checked.

name: Reka Flash 3
capabilitySummary: 21B open reasoning model from ex-DeepMind founders; Reka Core (2024) was their multimodal flagship. Pre-2026 facts from memory; not re-checked this session, and no 2026 release found.

name: DeepSeek LLM 67B
capabilitySummary: DeepSeek's first general chat LLM (7B/67B dense, open). LMArena 1185 (Sep 2026 snapshot) - a GPT-3.5-era baby form.

name: DeepSeek-Coder
capabilitySummary: First DeepSeek code models (1.3B-33B, open); seed of the coder line.

name: DeepSeek-V2
capabilitySummary: 236B MoE (21B active) introducing Multi-head Latent Attention; its ultra-low pricing ignited China's 2024 API price war.

name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2
capabilitySummary: Open MoE coder built on V2; first open model to rival GPT-4 Turbo on code at release. LMArena 1265.

name: DeepSeek-V2.5
capabilitySummary: Merged chat + coder lines into one model. LMArena 1307-1323.

name: DeepSeek-V3
capabilitySummary: 671B MoE (37B active) trained for a famously small compute budget; GPT-4o-class open model that set up the R1 shock. LMArena 1358; V3-0324 update 1396.

name: DeepSeek-R1
capabilitySummary: Open o1-level RL reasoning model; DeepSeek app passed ChatGPT as most-downloaded app (Jan 27, 2025) and Nvidia fell ~18% - the original 'DeepSeek moment'. R1-0528 update LMArena 1422.

name: DeepSeek-V3.1
capabilitySummary: Hybrid thinking/non-thinking model merging V3 and R1 lines, stronger tool use; V3.1-Terminus followed 2025-09-22. LMArena 1415-1417.

name: DeepSeek-V3.2
capabilitySummary: Production version of the DeepSeek Sparse Attention design (V3.2-Exp 2025-09-29); big long-context price cuts. LMArena 1425.

September added Sonnet 5.5 as the default Sonnet, --cloud sessions, a plugin portal and reading AGENTS.md. Mascot: Clawd, an orange 8-bit pixel crab.

name: Claude Cowork
capabilitySummary: A general desktop agent for non-coding work. It went GA for all paid plans on 2026-04-09, together with the Claude Managed Agents beta, and reached web and mobile on 2026-07-07. On 2026-09-16 it merged with Claude chat into a single Claude assistant 'superapp', alongside Claude Docs and Slides betas. Claude Code remains separate.

name: Project Mariner
capabilitySummary: Google's experimental Chrome web-browsing agent. It was shut down on 2026-05-04 and its technology folded into Gemini Agent and Chrome auto-browse. RETIRED.

name: Gemini Agent
capabilitySummary: The task-automation agent in the Gemini app: email triage, bookings and web tasks, now including Mariner's absorbed technology. The Gemini app grew from 750M MAU (Q4 2025) to 900M+ (I/O 2026) to about 950M (Q2 2026 earnings).

name: Gemini CLI
capabilitySummary: Google's open-source (Apache-2.0) terminal agent with 107k stars. Google announced at I/O 2026 that Gemini CLI would be replaced by Antigravity CLI, and it stopped serving free, Pro and Ultra consumers on 2026-06-18. Enterprise and API-key use continues, and the repo still ships (v0.60.0, 2026-09-15). One tracker still lists a free tier, which conflicts with Google's announcement.

name: Google Jules
capabilitySummary: An asynchronous GitHub coding agent that runs in cloud VMs and fixes bugs, writes tests and opens PRs. It was announced in Dec 2024 and reached GA in Aug 2025. It remains separate from Antigravity and can be orchestrated through a Gemini CLI extension.

name: Google Antigravity
capabilitySummary: An agent-first development platform. Antigravity 2.0 (I/O, 2026-05-19) spans a desktop app, a CLI (agy), an SDK, a Managed Agents API and an enterprise path, with parallel subagents, and it replaced Gemini CLI and Code Assist for consumers. It runs Gemini 3.8 Flash (2026-09-02; 87.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, model-level) plus Claude and gpt-oss. It has a free Individual tier; the app reached v2.16.0 on Sep 22. Google says 'millions of developers' use it. It was built largely by the ex-Windsurf team Google hired in July 2025.

name: NotebookLM
capabilitySummary: A source-grounded research notebook. NotebookLM 2.0 runs on Gemini 3.5 and, since June 2026, autonomously searches the web to add sources. Each notebook gets a secure cloud computer for code and charts. It exports editable PPT, Excel and PDF, and generates audio and video overviews, slides, flashcards and quizzes; it also integrates with Google Classroom.

name: Cursor
capabilitySummary: An agentic VS Code fork, described as the fastest-growing SaaS ever. ARR went from about $1B (Nov 2025) to $2B (Feb 2026) to $3B (May, Bloomberg) and about $4B (Jun) [reports]. SpaceX took an acquisition option on 2026-04-21 and closed the deal on 2026-08-14 for $60B in stock; Cursor now sits in SpaceXAI, with first-party Composer 2.5 and co-trained Grok 4.7. Aug-Sep 2026 brought Origin code hosting, always-on cloud agents with /goal, self-hosted runners and Projects (coordinator plus cloud subagents). Composer 2 (Mar 2026) was built on Kimi K2.5.

name: Windsurf
capabilitySummary: Codeium's agentic IDE, built around its Cascade agent. In July 2025 Google hired its leadership in a licensing deal and Cognition acquired the rest (about $82M ARR at the time). It was renamed Devin Desktop in June 2026.

name: Devin
capabilitySummary: The 'first AI software engineer', now available as Devin Web, Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) and Devin CLI. The SWE-2 model (2026-09-10, post-trained from Kimi K3) scores 50.0% on FrontierCode 1.1. Devin Fusion pairs a Fable 5.1 lead with a SWE-2 executor and ranks #2 on the AA Coding Agent Index (61.7). Cognition's ARR rose from about $492M (May 2026) to about $900M (Sep) [reported], at a $25B valuation (Apr 2026).

name: Replit Agent
capabilitySummary: A browser-based agent that builds and deploys full-stack apps. Agent 4 (Mar 2026) claims to be 10x faster than Agent 3. Replit raised a $400M Series D at a $9B valuation (Mar 2026), had about $525M ARR in Apr 2026 and is targeting $1B by year-end. It reports about 50M users.

name: Lovable
capabilitySummary: A Stockholm 'vibe coding' app builder. ARR hit $500M in Jun 2026 and was expected near $600M by end-Aug. It raised a $400M Series C at $13.3B on 2026-08-12, hosts 60M projects and has about 8M users [estimate].

name: Bolt.new
capabilitySummary: An in-browser full-stack app agent built on WebContainers. It went from $0 to about $40M ARR in roughly 5 months and has 5M+ users. A Microsoft Azure / M365 partnership followed in May 2026, and it claims 75% of the Fortune 500 as users.

name: v0
capabilitySummary: Vercel's generative UI and full-stack app agent. It had 4M+ users by Feb 2026 (other estimates say 6M developers and about $42M v0 ARR) [estimates]. Vercel overall crossed a $500M run-rate in July 2026.

name: Kiro
capabilitySummary: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE and CLI on credit plans (free 50 credits, $20 for 1,000). In September 2026 it shipped IDE 1.1 with ARM64 and CLI 2.22.0, and moved GPT-5.6 tiers to 1M context. It also supports Claude Sonnet 4.5 and open-weight models (Qwen3 Coder, DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM).

name: Grok Build
capabilitySummary: xAI's terminal coding agent. With Grok 4.7 it scores 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 56.3 on the AA Coding Agent Index (Sep 2026). Grok models have been co-trained with Cursor since the SpaceX deal. Launch month is approximate, based on a May 2026 Hacker News item.

name: OpenCode
capabilitySummary: The most-starred open-source coding agent (MIT), with 211k stars [verified via GitHub API, 2026-10-02]. It supports 75+ model providers and claims about 7.5M monthly developers. V2 shipped on 2026-09-11 with a new plugin API. OpenCode with GLM-5.3 scores 53.6 on the AA Coding Agent Index, the only open-source harness on that index. The Kilo CLI is a fork of OpenCode.

name: Cline
capabilitySummary: An Apache-2.0 agent for VS Code and JetBrains, plus a CLI and a macOS app, with 69.7k stars. Cline 4.0 (2026-06-26) moved to the shared SDK and added ClinePass ($9.99) for open models. v4.1.20 runs subagents in parallel. Roo Code, its fork, shut down on 2026-05-15.

name: OpenHands
capabilitySummary: An open-source (MIT) autonomous software-dev agent platform with SDK, CLI and cloud, at 89.8k stars [verified via GitHub API]. It started as OpenDevin, a community answer to Devin.

name: Trae
capabilitySummary: ByteDance's AI-native IDE. It had 1.6M MAU and 6M registered users by Dec 2025. A standalone SOLO version (desktop plus web) launched on 2026-03-31 with Code and MTC (More Than Coding) modes, free in China. The sibling TraeWork office agent competes with WorkBuddy and 千问办公.

name: CodeBuddy
capabilitySummary: Tencent's coding family: plugin, IDE (public beta Sep 2025) and the 'CodeBuddy Code' CLI. CodeBuddy Code 2.0 (2026-01-22) added Plan mode and a plugin market. On 2026-08-13 all CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy products moved to DeepSeek-V4-Pro, alongside Hunyuan.

name: 通义灵码
capabilitySummary: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen-based IDE coding assistant and China's early mass-market AI coder. It was officially renamed Qoder CN on 2026-05-20.

name: Qoder
capabilitySummary: Alibaba's agentic coding platform. Qoder 1.0 shipped in May 2026, and an Aug 2026 version went beyond a traditional IDE. The Qoder CN family includes the IDE, a JetBrains plugin, the QoderWork CN desktop app, a CLI, the QoderWake digital employee and Cloud Agents. The free Qwen 3.8 Flash period was extended on Sep 30, 2026, and it was featured at the Yunqi Conference (2026-09-22).

name: Manus
capabilitySummary: The general agent that kicked off the 2025 'agent' craze; Chinese-founded and Singapore-based. It passed $100M ARR by end-2025. Meta's deal ($2-3B, Dec 2025) was blocked by China's NDRC on 2026-04-27 and then unwound. Manus announced independence on Aug 11 and resumed independent operations on 2026-09-01.

name: Manus 2.0
capabilitySummary: A full re-architecture on the in-house 'Cascade' harness, which scales compute as projects grow (one test reported 32% lower cost). The app was renamed Manus Studio, 'a shared workspace for people and AI'. It launched alongside 'Cue', a standalone personal-agent app.

name: Genspark Super Agent
capabilitySummary: A mixture-of-agents super agent that orchestrates 150+ tools, mainly on Claude: slides, sheets, video, and real phone calls. It reached $250M ARR in 2026 and became a unicorn at $2.6B (Series B extension, 2026-06-17). Reported GAIA is about 75%.

name: Flowith
capabilitySummary: A canvas-style AI creation workspace. Agent Neo is a long-running, 'infinite-step', million-token-context creation agent; FlowithOS is a browser-based agentic OS; Knowledge Garden provides memory. The team's country of origin is unverified.

name: Perplexity
capabilitySummary: A cited answer engine and the leading AI-search challenger, with 100M+ MAU [reported]. Valuation was about $23B as of 2026-09-04, with Nvidia reportedly in talks at $30B. Revenue reportedly topped a $750M run-rate in Aug 2026 [aggregator].

name: Comet
capabilitySummary: Perplexity's agentic Chromium browser (research, form filling, shopping, booking). It has been free for everyone since 2025-10-02 and had about 3M MAU in Q1 2026 [estimate]. It expanded to iOS and more platforms on 2026-03-27. It outlived OpenAI's Atlas.

name: Perplexity Computer
capabilitySummary: A 'general-purpose digital worker' that orchestrates 19-20+ models end to end: research, design, code, deploy. It launched on Max first and reached Pro and Enterprise on 2026-03-12. An Enterprise edition with Slack and Snowflake connectors was announced at Ask 2026.

name: Character.AI
capabilitySummary: A character roleplay and companion platform with about 20M MAU in 2026 (down from a 28M peak in mid-2024). Users average about 75 min/day, and roughly 52% are aged 18-24. Open-ended chat for under-18s was removed in Nov 2025. Recent features include AvatarFX video, Scenes and Streams. Google struck a $2.7B licensing deal in 2024, and Karandeep Anand became CEO in June 2025.

name: Meta Muse
capabilitySummary: Meta's personal agent app, also usable inside WhatsApp. It turns long-term goals into plans, then browses, fills forms and negotiates on the user's behalf. Pricing is free plus $20 and $100 tiers. It hit #1 free on the App Store about 10 days after launch and has about 2.5M US downloads [reported]. Its sibling Muse Code terminal agent (beta 2026-08-05) scores 54.3 on the AA Coding Agent Index with Muse Spark 1.3.

name: Clawdbot
capabilitySummary: The original self-hosted 'assistant in your chat apps', first released as Warelay. After Anthropic trademark complaints it molted into Moltbot on 2026-01-27, and then into OpenClaw on 2026-01-30.

name: OpenClaw
capabilitySummary: A self-hosted personal agent runtime that lives in WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, iMessage and Teams (and WeChat/QQ via QClaw). It is the most-starred software project on GitHub: 391k stars [verified via GitHub API, 2026-10-02], passing React in Mar 2026. Its creator joined OpenAI and the project moved to the OpenClaw Foundation on 2026-02-14; v2.0 shipped on 2026-08-30. It triggered China's Spring Festival 2026 'lobster' craze, but Chinese authorities restricted its use in SOEs, government and banks in Mar 2026. Third-party skills carry real supply-chain risk. Mascot: Molty the space lobster.

name: Hermes Agent
capabilitySummary: A self-improving open-source (MIT) agent with persistent memory that learns its own skills from usage. It went viral weeks after OpenClaw as the agent that 'doesn't forget you'. It has 250.7k stars [verified via GitHub API, 2026-10-02]. Hermes Desktop was demoed in Jensen Huang's GTC keynote, and Bot mode supports multi-agent teams. Hosted tiers run $20-200/mo, and Nous was in talks at a $1.5B valuation in Jul 2026. It powers Tencent's LightVela cloud agent.

name: Moltbook
capabilitySummary: A Reddit-style social network where only AI agents (via OpenClaw) post and humans watch. It went viral in Jan 2026, partly because of fake posts enabled by an unsecured database. Meta acquired it on 2026-03-10, and the founders joined Meta Superintelligence Labs.

name: AutoGPT
capabilitySummary: The pioneering autonomous GPT-4 loop that ignited the 2023 agent hype. It is now a visual agent-builder platform with continuous agents, at 187.7k stars [verified via GitHub API].

name: LangChain
capabilitySummary: The most-downloaded agent framework, with 100M+ monthly downloads by Jun 2026 [reported] and 147k stars [verified]. It raised a $125M Series B at a $1.25B valuation in Oct 2025. LangSmith provides observability and evals.

name: LangGraph
capabilitySummary: A stateful, graph-based runtime for production agents, with about 34.5M monthly PyPI downloads (Sep 2026) and 42.6k stars. Deep Agents v0.6 and hosted Managed Deep Agents were announced at Interrupt 2026.

name: Dify
capabilitySummary: An open-source platform for LLM apps and agentic workflows (visual workflows, RAG, plugin marketplace) at 157.7k stars [verified via GitHub API]. It is widely self-hosted by enterprises, especially in China.

name: n8n
capabilitySummary: Fair-code workflow automation that became a mainstream AI-agent builder through its agent and LLM nodes. It has 206k stars [verified via GitHub API], one of the top AI-related repositories.

name: browser-use
capabilitySummary: An open-source library that lets LLM agents control real browsers. It is the de facto open web-agent layer, at 117k stars [verified via GitHub API].

name: Coze
capabilitySummary: ByteDance's agent-building platform; Coze Studio was open-sourced in Jul 2025 (21.7k stars). Coze 3.0 (2026-06-01) added multi-person, multi-agent project spaces and one-click OpenClaw / Claude Code integration. Agents get their own @coze.email address, cloud PCs and Android cloud phones, plus industry skill packs. It claims 100M+ agents running (Sep 2026).

name: 豆包 App
capabilitySummary: China's #1 AI app, with 382M MAU (QuestMobile, Jun 2026), about 2.3x 千问 and up 182% year on year (May). DAU passed 100M in Dec 2025. It runs Seed 2.0 (Feb 2026), Seed 2.1 and Seedance 2.5 video (Jun 2026). The 豆包手机助手 phone-operating agent launched in late 2025.

name: 豆包工作
capabilitySummary: ByteDance's productivity agent. It decomposes goals and drives multi-step work: reports, minutes, tables and analysis, plus images, video, web pages and apps. It is deeply integrated with Feishu and native in the 豆包 desktop app. The list price is 68元/月, but there were repeated 30-day free campaigns in Sep 2026, prompting subsidy wars with WorkBuddy and 千问办公.

name: 千问 App
capabilitySummary: Alibaba's consumer flagship, renamed from 通义. It has 167M MAU (QuestMobile, Jun 2026, #2), up 53x year on year (May). At the Yunqi Conference (2026-09-22) Alibaba pushed a Qwen 'Personal Agent' and launched the Qwen Intelligence AI-phone stack and QwenBook, an agent PC tied into Alipay.

name: 千问办公
capabilitySummary: Alibaba's enterprise agent combining desktop, cloud and collaborative agents with an Office suite, browser automation and scheduled tasks. It is integrated with DingTalk and consolidates QoderWork, MuleRun and 悟空. Qwen3.8 debuted here, and public beta opened on 2026-08-03.

name: 腾讯元宝
capabilitySummary: Tencent's AI assistant on Hunyuan plus DeepSeek, embedded across the WeChat ecosystem, with 49.84M MAU (QuestMobile, Jun 2026, #4 in China).

name: WorkBuddy / QClaw
capabilitySummary: WorkBuddy is Tencent's OpenClaw-compatible desktop workplace agent (20+ skill packages, multi-model, local install). It went global in May 2026 and moved to DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 2026-08-13. QClaw is a one-click OpenClaw installer and launcher bridging WeChat and QQ. A sibling, LightVela, is a Hermes-based 24/7 cloud agent (Apr 2026, WeChat/QQ/Feishu/WeCom) dubbed 'China's Muse'.

name: Kimi App
capabilitySummary: Moonshot's long-context assistant. App MAU slid to about 7.45M (QuestMobile, May 2026, down 47% year on year) as Moonshot pivoted to models and agents. Kimi K3 (2.8T MoE, released 2026-07-16, weights 2026-07-27) debuted #3 on Artificial Analysis. K3.1 was spotted in the API registry and teased around 2026-09-28 [rumored/unreleased].

name: Kimi Work
capabilitySummary: A local desktop multi-agent for knowledge workers. Its Agent Swarm scales to 300 sub-agents and 4,000 coordinated steps, and WebBridge drives logged-in browser sessions. Kimi Code is the sibling terminal and desktop coding agent (from $19/mo). It ran on K2.6/K2.7-Code and is now on K3.

name: DeepSeek App
capabilitySummary: It went #1 on the US App Store with R1 in Jan 2025. It has 130M MAU (QuestMobile, Jun 2026, #3), although MAU fell about 24% year on year in May. V4-Pro and V4-Flash shipped on 2026-04-24 as MIT open weights with 1M context, and V4-Pro reached GA in the app on 2026-08-13. Mascot: a blue whale; the fan persona '鲸鱼娘 / 大肥鱼' is popular.

name: AutoGLM
capabilitySummary: Zhipu's agent that operates phones and the web on the user's behalf (AutoGLM-Thinking, 50+ skills). Its sibling ZCode (2026-07-02) is a Claude Code-style coding harness running GLM-5.3 (2026-08-14), which Zhipu claims is the strongest open-weights coding model.

name: MiniMax Agent
capabilitySummary: MiniMax's general agent on web, mobile and desktop, with local-file batch processing. It runs MiniMax M3 (open-weight, 1M context, 2026-06-01). MiniMax Code reached v3.1.0 on 2026-09-30. Launch month is approximate.

name: Figure 03
capabilitySummary: A general-purpose humanoid running Helix 02, a vision-language-action model with whole-body autonomy (Jan 2026). It has tactile five-finger hands, palm cameras, 5h runtime and a 20kg payload. The BotQ factory builds about one per hour, with 350+ delivered. Paid fleets are at BMW Spartanburg (40 units) and Catalyst Brands.

name: Tesla Optimus
capabilitySummary: Tesla's humanoid robot. Optimus V3 (22-DoF hands, Fremont line) was promised for 2026 but had no formal reveal as of mid/late Sep 2026 [V3 unreleased]. Supply-chain reports cite parts for about 15k units in 2026. Optimus appeared at the Cybercab launch on 2026-09-03.

name: Unitree G1/H2
capabilitySummary: Agile low-cost humanoids famous for backflips and kung-fu demos. Unitree IPO'd on Shanghai's STAR market in Aug 2026, raising about $900M at about a $9B valuation, and the stock rose about 500% on day one. It shipped about 5,900 humanoids in H1 2026 (31% global share, #2).

name: AgiBot
capabilitySummary: The world's #1 humanoid vendor in H1 2026, with about 8,400 units (44% share), up 562% year on year. It passed 10,000 cumulative units in Jun 2026 and is pursuing a Hong Kong IPO. Products span the A-series bipedal, X-series compact and G-series wheeled robots. Co-founder 稚晖君 (Peng Zhihui) is a famous Bilibili tech creator.

name: 1X NEO
capabilitySummary: A soft, quiet home humanoid (1.65m, about 30kg) priced at $20k or $499/mo. Production started in Hayward, CA, with first US deliveries slated for 2026; actual delivery status is unverified.
